title.narrative: Provision of Emergency and Inclusive WASH Services for Drought Affected and Hard to Reach Populations in Afgooye district.

description.narrative: ltpgtPAH December 2025 needs assessment in Afgooye District revealed critical WASH gaps across IDP camps and rural village. Most households are displaced families living in overcrowded shelters with limited resources. Eighty nine percent lacked soap, only 46% practiced handwashing at critical times, and more than half reported insufficient water, with 86% paying high costs. Seventy one percent had no latrines, 20% practiced open defecation, and 98% lacked waste disposal sites, resorting to unsafe methods. These conditions expose communities especially women and children to heightened risks of AWD, cholera, and protection concerns.ltbrgtTo respond to these urgent needs, Polish Humanitarian Action (PAH) proposes an 8-month standalone WASH intervention that will reach approximately 13,476 individuals (2,695Men, 3639 women, 3099 boys and 4043 girls) as well as people with disabilities and other vulnerable groups in 6 IDP camps and 5 rural villages in Afgooye District. The intervention will also strengthen collaboration with other sectors, including Health, Nutrition, and Food Security partners selected under the reserved allocation. The project will deliver lifesaving and sustainable WASH activities, prioritized as immediate needs. These activities are aligned with Reserve Allocation priorities and will comprise the following:ltbrgt Restoring safe water access: PAH will provide emergency water to vulnerable IDPs through Water trucking, public/private borehole engagement, rehabilitation of water supply (2 shallow wells and 1 boreholes) through desilting and installation of solar panels and a submersible pump, plus construction of a new elevated 20MC storage tank and caretaker rooms. To ensure quality and sustainability, all works will follow the Somalia WASH Toolkit and UNICEF Somalia WASH Road Map 2020-2025, covering design, construction, operation, and maintenance standards. Chlorination, water quality monitoring, and household level chlorination will be conducted regularly to safeguard public health. Gender balanced water management committees will be established and trained to oversee daily functionality, preventive maintenance, and long-term sustainability.ltbrgt Expanding emergency sanitation: The project will construct 65 flood resistant communal latrines, with at least 15% adapted for people with disabilities (10 units). Portable solar lights will be provided to reduce GBV risks, particularly for women and girls at night. PAH will pilot household kettles as a practical and sustainable handwashing solution. Sitting and design will be informed by protection assessments and community consultations, with sanitation materials distributed for ongoing maintenance.ltbrgt Promoting inclusive hygiene and risk communication: PAH will deploy 11 trained hygiene promoters and 4 community mobilizers to conduct structured door to door visits and community dialogues. Messaging will emphasize hand hygiene, latrine care, safe water handling, menstrual hygiene management (MHM), and PSEA awareness, using Somalia WASH Cluster approved materials. Sanitation tools will be distributed, two waste disposal pits excavated, and quarterly cleaning campaigns conducted.ltbrgtTo ensure accountability and learning, Post Distribution Monitoring (PDM) for hygiene kits(1000HH) will be conducted alongside regular project monitoring. The project will establish and publicize functional complaint and feedback mechanisms (CFMs), conduct inclusive beneficiary targeting through community structures, and involve women, persons with disabilities, and minority group leaders in project design, monitoring, and delivery. Field teams will coordinate closely with the WASH Cluster, Protection Cluster, ABC platforms, and local authorities to ensure strategic convergence and harmonized service coverage.ltbrgtlt/pgt
